subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, and operators?
rationale: The current Gateway has event primitives that could support observation, but exposing cross-channel transcript activity changes privacy, authorization, and public CLI/config expectations.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core observer mode
options.body: Keep raw logs, session tools, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid core cross-channel TUI mirroring.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue needs product/security boundary ownership for core TUI behavior, and recent TUI session lifecycle history points to this account as the best available routing candidate.
